transcript.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining today's pre-authorization review. As we all know, a student research team has proposed an online survey of first-year students about their transition to college, and before I can give final authorization and record the operating conditions, I need to hear from each of you. The draft proposal describes an anonymous survey, indefinite retention of responses, an open invitation to all first-year students, and eligibility for a public research presentation. I'd like to go through any conditions that should be included before we proceed. Could we start with the research coordinator's assessment?

transcript.text: I need to flag an important technical issue. I tested the survey platform and confirmed that it collects respondent email addresses by default. The launch settings must disable email collection and delete the existing test responses before student data are gathered. I recorded this in the platform test log, which is kept separate from the draft proposal, so this wouldn't have been visible in the proposal materials you've all seen.

transcript.text: Thank you, Elias. I need to flag a critical privacy concern. My policy review found that the survey includes questions about mental-health treatment and immigration status, which are classified as sensitive student data. Because of this, the project requires three specific conditions: explicit written consent from respondents, encrypted institutional storage of the responses, and deletion of all research responses exactly 30 days after collection closes. I entered this determination in the privacy review system, which is separate from the research proposal, so this wouldn't have been visible in the proposal materials any of you have seen. These conditions directly conflict with the draft proposal's description of an anonymous survey and indefinite retention of responses.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share an important constraint from the faculty mentoring record, which has not yet been attached to the proposal. The course attached to this project awards credit only for a study capped at exactly 100 enrolled respondents, and it permits dissemination only at the closed university undergraduate symposium, not at a public presentation. These conditions directly conflict with the draft proposal's open invitation to all first-year students and its stated eligibility for a public research presentation.
transcript.speaker: A4

commitments.detail: Email collection must be disabled on the survey platform before launch, and all existing test responses must be deleted prior to data collection.
Explicit written consent must be obtained from all respondents due to the inclusion of sensitive questions about mental-health treatment and immigration status.
All research responses must be stored in encrypted institutional storage and deleted exactly 30 days after collection closes, superseding the draft proposal's indefinite retention plan.
The survey must be capped at exactly 100 enrolled respondents, superseding the draft proposal's open invitation to all first-year students.
Results may be presented only at the closed university undergraduate symposium, not at any public presentation, superseding the draft proposal's stated eligibility.
